description: This image displays three pie charts, each representing the distribution of four categories labeled N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K− across three difficulty levels: “easy,” “medium,” and “hard.” The “easy” chart shows the largest segment, 55.4%, colored teal (N+K+), followed by 38.3% in yellow (N−K+), 4.6% in orange (N−K−), and 1.7% in red (N+K−). The “medium” chart has the largest segment at 58.8%, also teal (N+K+), followed by 35.4% in yellow (N−K+), 4.8% in orange (N−K−), and 1.8% in red (N+K−). The “hard” chart shows the largest segment at 37.9%, colored orange (N−K−), followed by 37.3% in yellow (N−K+), 18.1% in teal (N+K+), and 6.7% in red (N+K−). A legend on the right side confirms the color coding for each category. Each pie chart includes percentage labels inside its respective slices, and the slices are arranged in descending order of size within each chart.
